01 · THE SHIFT

Your next customer is a machine

There are two roles. The merchant is the store that publishes its products. The shopping agent is software that finds and compares products for a shopper. The agent doesn't browse your shopfront. It reads your data and picks an offer.

💸
$14.8m ILLUSTRATIVE

of loyal spend a year that an AI agent could move, for a retailer with 100,000 members spending $400 a year.

<WHAT AN AGENT MEETS AT A STORE BUILT FOR HUMANS/>

🤖

It reads data, not pages

Banners, photos and persuasive copy don't reach it. Structured product data does.

🏷️

Price is the loudest signal

Price alone doesn't tell the whole story, but it's often the only thing the agent can compare.

📄

Your advantages hide in prose

Easier returns, a longer warranty, a loyalty programme: all buried in policy documents.

❓

It can't check your claims

A benefit with no conditions and no evidence attached is just words to an agent.

05 · THREE IDEAS THAT MAKE IT WORK

Publish. Verify. Let the agent choose.

💬
1 · Publish

Speak the agent's language

A common language agents and stores already share. BondLayer speaks it for you.

Basic agents still read your catalogue. Benefit evidence is opt-in.

🔏
2 · Verify

Seal the real terms

Like a signed, sealed letter: the agent can see who wrote it and whether a single word has changed.

AI drafts each benefit from your policy and you approve it. The signature then covers its facts, conditions and source text.

A seal proves who said it, not that it's true. Merchant review still matters.

⚖️
3 · Choose

Code checks. Agent chooses.

Like a referee and a player: code enforces the rules, and the shopper's agent makes the call.

CODEChecks the products exist, signatures verify and conditions apply
LIVE MODELRanks the known offers using that evidence
CHECKOUTRe-checks every benefit record the agent cited

Effective cost is a reference figure, not the live ranking rule or the checkout price.

The merchant publishes the evidence. It does not buy the agent's ranking.
💬
1 · PUBLISH · IN DETAIL

Where BondLayer plugs into UCP

1

The business platform is the merchant's side

BondLayer runs this box for a retailer. It publishes a business profile: what the store supports, plus the public keys agents use to check signatures.

GET /{merchant}/.well-known/ucp
2

Standard capabilities it serves

Catalogue search and lookup, and checkout: the same features any UCP store offers.

catalog.search · catalog.lookup · dev.ucp.shopping.checkout
3

Our extensions

benefit_value attaches signed benefit records to catalogue results. intent_match lets an agent send the shopper's sentence and get proposals with reasons. Both live under org.bondlayer.*, because dev.ucp.* is reserved for the UCP Tech Council.

4

Transport

Plain HTTP (REST) today, built against the UCP draft dated 2026-04-08.

How an agent and a store agree

  1. The agent lists what it understands in the UCP-Agent header.
  2. The store keeps only the names and versions both sides support.
  3. An extension whose parent capability didn't survive is dropped.
  4. Declared nothing extra? The agent still gets the plain catalogue. The intent route answers 406.
🔏
2 · VERIFY · IN DETAIL

The life of a benefit record

1

Policy document

The retailer's returns, warranty, delivery or loyalty terms. The original text is kept.

2

Draft

A structured draft: the benefit, which products it covers, its conditions, and the exact source passage it came from.

3

Merchant review YOU DECIDE

Edit, approve or reject each draft. Nothing is signed without approval.

4

Sign

The record is written in one exact form (canonical JSON: same bytes every time), then signed with the merchant's private key, which never leaves the server.

ES256 · P-256 / SHA-256 · detached signature
5

Publish and verify

The public key sits in the merchant profile. An agent rebuilds the canonical form and checks the signature, and checkout checks it again.

/.well-known/ucp → signing_keys[]

What tampering looks like

Change one fact after signing and the check fails.

returns window: 60 days✓ verifies
returns window: 90 days✗ signature fails

Illustration of the check, not a real record.

Why sign the record, not just the message?

HTTPS and UCP's message signatures protect one response in transit. A signed record outlives that response: an agent can cache it, re-verify it later, and cite it at checkout.

What a seal does not prove

That the claim is true, or that a key belongs to who you think. That's why merchant review and published keys matter, and why unverified records earn no credit.

⚖️
3 · CHOOSE · IN DETAIL

From checked evidence to a confirmed order

1 · UNDERSTAND

Read the request

The shopper's sentence becomes separate requirements: hard, soft, service and values.

2 · CODE

Check the evidence

Only known (merchant, SKU) offers. Signatures verify, records haven't expired, scope applies. Unverified claims earn no credit.

3 · LIVE MODEL

Rank the offers

Orders the checked offers using summaries of the evidence. It can only pick from that list.

4 · CODE

Guard the answer

A pick outside the known list is an error, never a fabricated winner.

5 · CHECKOUT

Re-check and confirm

Each cited record must be the merchant's own, signed, unexpired, verified against its key and apply to an item. No money moves.

Effective cost: a reference, not the rule

Shelf price minus credited benefit value. Credit is capped by the merchant's declared ceiling and by the shopper's own valuation.

Voltway shelf price$1,142.96
Credited verified benefits− $209.95
Effective comparison cost$933.01

Recorded R01 reference result in rules mode. A live model's ordering can differ.

The honest limits

  • The model sees summaries of cited evidence, not every original policy fact.
  • Unverified entries are marked and the model is told to ignore them. That's an instruction, not a formal guarantee.
  • The deterministic rules (no credit for unverified claims, ceilings never override the shopper) are enforced by tests: tests/test_invariants.py.

Every issue is explained by its consequence. A price written "$1,099.00" means an agent filtering "under $1,500" would drop that listing.

Confirm

The agent names the benefits it relied on. The store re-checks each one: its own, signed, unexpired, and it applies to an item. Then it confirms. No money moves in this prototype.

POST /{merchant}/ucp/checkout

🔒 Stays with the shopper's agent

What each benefit is worth to this shopper, and the comparison across stores. No merchant can price against it.

📨 What the store receives

Search filters, then product IDs, quantities and the benefit IDs cited. It gets the shopper's sentence only if both sides opt in to intent matching, which returns proposals with a reason for each match.

10 · TRUST · WHY AN AGENT CAN RELY ON THIS

Verified can count. Unverified earns nothing.

✅

SIGNED + PRICED

recordvw-returns-60
typereturns
ceilingdeclared by merchant
seal✓ verifies

→ Credited, but capped twice: by the merchant's declared ceiling and by the shopper's own valuation.

🔧

SIGNED, NO PRICE

recordvw-repairability-parts-5y
typerepairability
ceilingnone
seal✓ verifies

→ Answers the shopper's repair preference. Worth exactly $0 in the price comparison.

🚫

UNVERIFIED

recordany claim
type"best warranty around"
ceilingn/a
seal✗ missing or fails

→ May be displayed, never credited. A record that can't be verified can't move a ranking.

🧪 Enforced by tests, not by slides

tests/test_invariants.py checks that unverified claims earn no credit and that a merchant's ceiling never overrides the shopper's valuation. At checkout, an order only binds records the store can re-verify against its own published key.

🔒 The shopper's priorities never leave the agent

What a benefit is worth to this shopper is never sent to a merchant. If checkout receives an extra field like shopper_policy, it answers 422: refused rather than quietly reading it.

11 · MARKET STRATEGY

Protocols carry the data. We make benefits checkable.

🎯 Who it's for

$14.8m ILLUSTRATIVE

Mid-market retailers with a catalogue export, a policy PDF and no integration team. Loyal spend an agent could move: 100,000 members × $400 × 37% (Accenture 2026).

💳 How it could earn PROPOSED

A hosted publishing layer on a per-merchant subscription, priced on request volume and catalogue size, not a share of sales. A merchant pays to be readable, not for influence over the ranking.

🚚 How we'd reach them PROPOSED

Systems integrators already doing retail transformation, with FPT's retail delivery practice first. Then e-commerce agencies. Later, a UCP platform listing once adoption evidence exists.

12 · WHERE IT STANDS · WHERE IT GOES

A working prototype, honestly scoped

✅ Works today

  • 🏪New merchant onboarding: business details, CSV upload, preview report, publish
  • 🔎Catalogue checks: accepted products are searchable; diagnostics explain repairs and remaining issues
  • 💾Saved merchants load again after a restart
  • 🤖Buyer-agent demo discovers stores on the server and compares their uploaded products
  • 🔏Signed benefits, ranking and checkout confirmation run end to end on the bundled demo stores

🚧 Not yet, and we say so

  • 📈No change in ranking (GEO): BondLayer doesn't optimise or buy a place in an agent's ranking. The agent still decides.
  • 💳Payment and order management: checkout confirms; no money moves
  • 🔐Production auth, live integrations, protocol certification. The eval ships 30 requests, not 100+.
